key: About the holy Law toils Savitar the God the horn of holy Law hath he spread far and wide. The holy Law hath quelled even mighty men of war.
s: In a hymn begging the Asvins to keep their friendship, the last verse turns to Savitar; Sāyaṇa, on 8.75.5, reads ‘holy Law’ as truth, by which Savitar quiets his rays at evening, and which by itself overcomes even an enemy’s great strength.

evidence.gloss: The seer makes a praise of truth. O Aśvins, the god, shining Savitar, who impels all to their own work, by ṛta, by truth, at evening quiets the mass of his rays. After that the same Savitar in the morning spreads wide the tip of ṛta, of truth. Moreover ṛta, truth, by itself overcomes even the great strength of a foe eager for battle.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Rig Veda 8.75.5 at [694,5]; standard 8.86.5); last verse of the hymn, whose refrain begs the Aśvins not to break friendship (Anukramaṇī: deity Aśvins). Sāyaṇa on 8.86.5 glosses ṛta as satya, says Savitar by truth quiets his rays at evening, and that truth by itself overcomes even a hostile warrior’s great strength, calling the verse a praise of truth (Wilson note 4 reports the same). Sentence carries exactly this; two words of the key quoted; entry-check ok. Revision 209020 dated 2019-08-08 by the Wikisource API.
